`0.svg` was an empty SVG with no drawing in it, so I only made its structure more robust and did not add artwork. The result is not machine-validated: my well-formedness check with `xmllint` was blocked because this session cannot approve that command.

The original file was this single line:

```
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"/>
```

It now reads:

```
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="300" height="150" viewBox="0 0 300 150" aria-hidden="true">
</svg>
```

- **Explicit size:** The width and height match the 300 by 150 default that browsers already used, so rendering does not change.
- **Scalable coordinate system:** The `viewBox` lets any future content scale cleanly when the image is resized.
- **Accessibility:** The image is hidden from screen readers, since an empty graphic has nothing to announce. Remove that attribute and add a `<title>` once there is real content.
- **Open root element:** The tag is no longer self-closing, so content can be added directly inside it.

I assumed "improve" meant tidying the file as it stands. If you wanted an actual graphic, such as a drawing of the digit zero, tell me what it should depict and at what size.
